narrative: Material PL1__M8DEF1B0 exhibits continuous moderate-variability demand (CV=0.51) with no detectable trend across 209 working days. Lead times are extremely short on average (0.088 WD) but highly variable (CV=0.99), which drives a meaningful safety stock requirement of 130 units to achieve the 95% service level target. The EOQ of 443 units — enforced above the MOQ of 193 — optimally balances ordering and holding costs, yielding a 5.1% annual cost reduction versus the current SAP policy while remaining well within the 2,619-unit storage constraint.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Continuous demand with ~93% non-zero daily activity and sub-day replenishment lead times make a continuous-review (r,Q) model the natural fit. The fixed order quantity (EOQ-derived, MOQ-constrained) minimises total ordering and holding costs, while the reorder point encodes the safety stock needed to buffer lead-time and demand variability.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity of 443 + safety stock of 130 = 573 units, well within the 2,619-unit storage cap. No capacity binding. If demand increases by >4x or safety stock is raised significantly, the cap may become binding.
